title: Not this, but that: nem … hanem

sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: To correct a mistake, say what is wrong with *nem* and what is right with *hanem* (“but rather”). *Nem* goes right before the wrong word: *Nem Anna főz, hanem Károly.* means “It is not Anna who cooks but Károly.” A comma goes before *hanem*.

sections.title: True or not true
sections.content: To say that a statement is not true, use *Nem igaz.* (*igaz* means “true”). Then give the correction: *Nem igaz! Nem Anna főz, hanem Károly.* *Igaz?* asks “Is that true?”

sections.title: Nem … hanem …
rows: It is not Anna who cooks but Károly.
Nem otthon olvasok, hanem a kertben.
I read not at home but in the garden.
I study not in the morning but in the evening.
It is not Meg who writes but Mariann.

items.spanish: Anna főz? – Nem Anna főz, hanem Károly.
items.english: Does Anna cook? – It is not Anna who cooks but Károly.

items.spanish: Nem a kertben olvasok, hanem otthon.
items.english: I read not in the garden but at home.
Is that true? – Yes, it is true.

sections.content: *Hanem* needs a *nem* before it. Do not swap it for *mert* or *és*: *Nem Anna főz, mert Károly* says something quite different.
